visualFeatures.feature: Calendar grid: weeks as columns, days as rows
visualFeatures.detail: CSS grid, grid-auto-flow: column, 7 rows. Monday is the top row and Sunday the bottom. 364 cells, which is 52 full weeks, and the first cell is a Monday. There is no leading or trailing padding. The grid sits centred inside a bordered 'well'.
border-radius 999px, so the ends are semicircles. Width:height is a constant 0.58 (h = 1.724 x w) in every instance, for example 19.47x33.58, 15x25.86, 11.69x20.15 and 7.29x12.57.

visualFeatures.feature: Square cells ('Support tickets · square cells', pin step 03 'Shape')
visualFeatures.detail: Same 0.58 aspect (tall rectangles, not true squares), border-radius a fixed 3px. The spec claims 'Four treatments from square to capsule, with density and corner radius driven together so the grid never reads as a stack of pills at high density'. A Cell shape slider runs Round to Square, with the default at 22% = 'Round'.

Default gap 3.16px ('Balanced', slider at 52%). 'Dense' / high density = 1px. Other gaps seen: 5px (landing ghost), 2.6px (landing chart), 2.1px (drawer preview), 2px (setup intent thumbnails). Copy: 'Loose to read. Tight to compare.' and 'The gap between cells is yours to set'.

visualFeatures.feature: Height-driven cell size, derived week count
visualFeatures.detail: The cell height is solved from the available height (7h + 6g = well inner height), the width is 0.58h, and weeks shown = floor((width + g)/(w + g)), capped at 52. Evidence: short box 44 weeks at 13px cells, tall box 19 weeks at 37px cells, pin stage 23 to 24 weeks, drawer 37 weeks, full screen 'Weeks shown 35 · derived', small multiples 45 weeks. Copy: 'a cell is never stretched to fill a box'. In the mock, fewer weeks still show the whole Jan to Dec trend compressed and keep the Jan..Nov labels, so the mock does not show which weeks a real truncation would keep.

Five-step sequential ramp plus an 'empty' colour for no-data days. The panel shows 'Steps 5' on a 3 to 9 slider and 'Bins 5 · quantile'. The spec claims 'Bin count from three to nine, or continuous'. The observed counts are NOT quantile, though. Sales has 37/106/93/45/8 active days across bins 1 to 5 plus 75 empty, and Sessions never uses bin 1. That pattern looks like equal-interval thresholds over 0..max.

visualFeatures.feature: Blank days render as empty, never zero
visualFeatures.detail: No-data days use var(--empty), a 5% ink tint (#f3f3f3 on white), rather than the lowest ramp step. The 'Show days with no data' toggle is on in the mock. The hint reads: 'Off leaves a gap, which reads as "no data" rather than "zero"'. Active days KPI: '289 / 364'.

.grid i.pk has box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1.8px var(--ink). That is #17151d in light and #f6f4fa in dark, drawn inside the cell, and the cell keeps its fill (#504a67). Sales peak = cell index 345 (week column 50 of 52, Wednesday row), labelled '16 Dec'. Sessions peak = index 362 (last week, Saturday). On the product page the ringed cell renders 23px wide against 15px siblings, which widens its week column and leaves a visible gap. The home page does not do this, so treat the home-page inset ring as canonical. Settings: 'Mark the peak day' toggle; KPI 'Dec · marked'.

Always the six labels Jan, Mar, May, Jul, Sep, Nov at 10px, ink3. They are spread evenly (flex:1, each 1/6 of the well width) starting at the well's left edge, NOT placed at real month-start weeks. They appear unchanged even on 19-week grids. Row height 13px with a 5px gap above the well. A 'Month labels' toggle exists. 'Month separators' toggle exists (off), with no separator drawn.

Only M, W, F, S, in a 15px column 6px left of the well, 9.5px ink3. They are justified space-between over the grid height, so they sit on rows 0, 2, 4, 6 (Mon, Wed, Fri, Sun). Setting: 'Day-of-week labels M · W · F · S'.
Footer left: 'Less' then five 11x11 swatches (radius 3, gap 3) then 'More', 12.5px ink3, gap 6px. A 'Legend' toggle exists.

Header row: title (Sora 600 15px, e.g. 'Sales'), subtitle 'by Order Date' (12.5px ink3), and a right-aligned total '1.33M' (600 15px, tabular numerals). Other totals: 847K Sessions, 10K Tickets, 3.85M split by Region.

Footer right: a 14px green circle (#1f8f6f) with a white check, 'Contrast checks out' in ink3, and '8.35:1' in mono 11.5px 600 ink2. The value is the WCAG contrast of the deepest step #504a67 against the well #ffffff, which I verified as 8.345. In dark it is '12.00:1' (#d1ccdc against #12101a, verified 12.004).
On selection the chip text changes to 'Filtered to week 29' ('week 29' in mono bold). The selected week is cells 196 to 202 (week column 29).

visualFeatures.detail: A 2x2 grid of panels (North 1.33M, South 1.09M, EMEA 835K, APAC 595K), each 45 weeks with no month or weekday labels. One shared legend. Chip 'One shared scale · 45 weeks in every panel'. Panel: Split by Region, Columns 2 (1..4), Panel titles; the section is locked. Tag 'Designed · not shipped'.
'Week starts: Monday' dropdown. The standard card shows MON / SUN / SAT start rows with the weekend positions moving. Spec: 'Any week start'.
Spec: 'calendar or fiscal year'. The report is titled 'Daily Sales · FY26' with a filter 'Year · FY26'.
'leap years handled rather than approximated'; 'Week starts, fiscal years, time zones, leap years'.
Layout 'Granularity: Day' dropdown; copy 'whether you are looking at days, weeks or months'.
'Sum, average, min, max, count and distinct count, applied per day'; the dropdown shows Sum.
'Tested from a 200-pixel tile up to full-page, and at ten years of daily data.' 'Static-image export and PDF supported.'
'One week of data. A 200-pixel tile. A year with gaps in it.' Illustrated with three dashed mini bar tiles labelled 1 WEEK, 200PX TILE and GAPS.

visualFeatures.feature: Dark theme inversion / follows report theme
visualFeatures.detail: In dark mode the ramp inverts: low values are darkest, nearest the canvas, and high values are light. Dark ramp #362d51 to #d1ccdc on well #12101a. Empty is #f6f4fa at 5%, and the peak ring becomes light. Toggles 'Match the report theme' (on) and 'Reverse the ramp' (off). I captured dark versions of every mock.

Drawer groups: RECOMMENDED Signature; BOARD-SAFE Neutral, Classic blue, Grayscale ('Low-saturation ramps that survive a projector and a printer.'); HIGH-SIGNAL Coral, Amber ('Warm and bright, good when the point is to draw the eye.'); COLOUR-BLIND SAFE Teal, Green. The showcase picker offers Signature, Ember, Forest and Slate. Claims: 'Ten palettes in four groups', plus a custom ramp; the spec says 'Five sequential palettes, a diverging palette, a colour-blind-safe categorical set, and a custom ramp'.

'Accessibility · 2 of 4 passing': ✓ Deepest step vs the heatmap area 8.35:1; ! Steps are evenly spaced 2.9x; ✓ Lightness moves one way Monotonic; ! A second channel for magnitude Colour only. The check mark uses ok #1f8f6f and the '!' uses warn #9c7a3f. Also claimed: ramp mixed in gamma space, and palettes checked against three colour-vision deficiencies.

visualFeatures.feature: Screen reader, keyboard, high contrast, reduce motion
visualFeatures.detail: Spec: 'Keyboard navigable, high-contrast mode honoured, screen-reader labels per cell'. Advanced page: Reduce motion toggle; High-contrast mode 'Follow Windows'.

Advanced: 'Value format: Compact (1.3M)'. The format is not consistent across the mocks: the visual's KPI strip uses lowercase k with one decimal (3.6k, 11.6k, 188.2k), while the report mock and header totals use 1.33M, 3.6K, 12K and 847K.
'Applies the Hichert SUCCESS preset in one move; locks typography, spacing and the comparison notation.'

Header: calendar icon, 'Lumeric Calendar Heatmap' / 'Sales by Order Date', and undo, redo, expand and close icons. Then a live mini preview; a status line 'Signature · Balanced · Round' with a green '• Live'; 'Search settings'; a back arrow and section title; grouped setting boxes (card2 bg, radius 12); a lock icon on Palette; footer '🔒 1 locked'.

A settings rail (Design, Color, Layout, Data & analytics, Small multiples 🔒, Race playback, Interaction, Advanced | Suggestions 2, Review changes 4), the current page, and a live preview with the accessibility card. Footer: 'Contrast 8.35:1' ... 'Preset Signature · Weeks shown 35 · 1 changed from the preset'.

Changes grouped by section with the old value struck through, an arrow, then the new value in bold. 'Not on the report yet 2 [Apply all] [Discard]': Match the report theme On→Off, Palette Signature→Neutral. 'Design 2 [Clear section]': Density Balanced→Dense, Show days with no data On→Off. Undo and redo in the header.
Tagged cards (READABILITY, POLISH), each with a reason, an action button and Dismiss. Every suggestion writes a real setting and can be undone.
Preset 'Signature'; tone 'Balanced · Round' moves palette, density and cell shape together. Governance is per section ('1 locked', Small multiples locked).

Landing: a ghost grid behind the text 'LUMERIC / Calendar Heatmap', with buttons [Set it up →] and [Use defaults]. Then 1 Intent (4 cards: Lumeric Signature 'Distinctive, built for dashboards' = Signature; Executive 'Clean, restrained, board-ready' = Slate; Analytical 'Dense, information-rich' = Forest; Presentation 'Spacious, presentation-ready' = Ember), 2 Appearance (Density and Cell shape sliders beside a live preview), 3 Done ('Open Calendar Heatmap →'). 'Skip for now'.
@keyframes cellIn: scale .5→1 and opacity 0→1 over .5s, with a 9ms stagger per week column. Only the page 'Four decisions' stage stays pinned while scrolling.
No external service calls, no remote resources, under the code-size budget, reviewed for data privacy. The spec admits it is 'not certified yet'.

inventory.cellGeometry:
Grid:
- CSS grid, 7 rows, auto-flow column (one column per week). Monday is the top row and Sunday the bottom.
- 364 cells = 52 weeks, and the data begins on a Monday. No padding cells.

Cell aspect:
- Width:height = 0.58 everywhere, so height = 1.724 x width. Examples: 19.47x33.58, 15x25.86, 11.69x20.15, 6.22x10.72, 23.2x40.
- The size captions quote height ('cell 13px' = 13.01 tall).

Corner radius:
- Capsule: 999px, i.e. radius = width/2.
- 'Square': a fixed 3px.

Gap:
- 3.16px default ('Balanced').
- 1px 'Dense'.
- 2 to 2.6px in small previews, 5px in the landing ghost.

Sizing rule:
- Solve h from the well height (7h + 6g = inner height).
- w = 0.58h.
- Weeks shown = floor((innerWidth + g)/(w + g)), max 52. Verified exactly for 44 and 19 weeks.
- When all 52 fit, the well shrinks to the grid and centres.

Well:
- White (#fff light, #12101a dark), 1px border #17151d0e, radius 11px.
- The grid is centred with about 4px inset per side inside the 1px border: 1184x264 well for a 1173.6x254 grid.

Weekday labels:
- 15px column, 6px gap to the well.
- M, W, F, S justified space-between over the grid height, so they fall on rows 0, 2, 4, 6.

Month labels:
- A row 13px tall, 5px above the well. Padding-left 22px so it starts at the well edge.
- Six spans (Jan, Mar, May, Jul, Sep, Nov), each flex:1 = 1/6 of the width. Evenly spaced, not date-aligned.

Legend:
- Footer 14px below the well.

Peak ring:
- An inset box-shadow of 1.8px in the ink colour (#17151d light, #f6f4fa dark), same radius as the cell, fill unchanged (#504a67).
- In Vega: a second rect at x+0.9, y+0.9, w-1.8, h-1.8 with stroke 1.8 and the same cornerRadius.

Selection:
- Unselected cells get opacity .24.

capabilities.topic: Single-click cross-filter on a data point
capabilities.detail: Set objects.vega enableSelection true (default false). In simple mode (selectionMode 'simple', the default) Deneb binds a 'click' listener to the Vega view, resolves the clicked mark's datum to a dataset row through __row__ (field-value matching is the fallback), and passes that row's selection ID to Power BI's ISelectionManager. Works in both Vega and Vega-Lite. The spec has to style selection state itself from the per-row __selected__ field ('on' / 'off' / 'neutral'). Row context has to survive: a Vega formula or filter on a derived source dataset keeps __row__, but aggregate transforms lose it, and primitive-aggregate resolution is only best effort. A calendar cell that is one date row is the ideal case. Whether other visuals filter or highlight is set in Power BI's Edit interactions, not by Deneb. It also needs host.allowInteractions, which is false in some hosts such as dashboard tiles.

capabilities.topic: Drag a date range and cross-filter the rest of the report
capabilities.detail: This is possible only in Vega, with selectionMode 'advanced'. Mechanism: keep the drag endpoints in TOP-LEVEL signals (for example brushLo and brushHi, set on mousedown and mousemove over the cell mark). On mouseup, call pbiCrossFilterApply(event, "datum['Date'] >= brushLo && datum['Date'] <= brushHi", {limit: 2500}). Power BI never receives the filter as an expression. Deneb runs it in a headless Vega view over the base dataset, collects the matching rows' __row__ and selects their selection IDs. That headless view copies only top-level signal values (event.dataflow._signals), so signals inside group marks are invisible to it. The range is therefore carried as a list of row identities, with a hard cap of 2,500 rows (options.limit 1-2500; the default is 50 if omitted). At daily grain that is about 6.8 years per selection. A 10-year drag goes over the cap, and so does any extra grouping column that multiplies rows per day. Deneb then returns {exceedsLimit: true}, keeps the previous selection and shows the header warning. The spec can read that return value if the apply call's result is stored in a signal. Deneb has no JSON or Advanced filter API: applyJsonFilter appears nowhere in the 2.0.0.0 source. So a true 'between dates' filter is impossible, as are filter-pane persistence and cross-page sync. Other visuals receive a normal cross-filter or cross-highlight, as set in Edit interactions. Checked offline with Vega 6.4.0: relational comparisons (>=, <=) on Date objects work. == on Date objects never matches (it compares object identity). That includes the documented placeholder form datum['Date'] == _{Date}_, which Deneb resolves to toDate('<ISO>'); use time(datum['Date']) == time(_{Date}_) instead. Call apply once on mouseup, not on every mousemove. The DAX cost to other visuals of a 2,500-identity selection has not been measured, and none of this has been reproduced in Desktop.

capabilities.topic: Cross-highlight (receiving highlights from other visuals), __highlight__ fields
capabilities.detail: Set enableHighlight true. Each MEASURE gets <measure>__highlight, the value for the highlighted subset, which equals the base value when nothing is highlighted. On 1.9 and on migrated visuals, measures also get __highlightStatus ('neutral'/'on'/'off') and __highlightComparator ('eq'/'lt'/'gt'/'neq'); on new 2.0 projects those two are opt-in through supportFieldConfiguration. Columns never get highlight fields. The spec has to draw 'two visuals in one', for example base intensity dimmed with highlight intensity on top, or opacity driven by the highlight/base ratio. Each source visual's Edit interactions setting decides whether it highlights or filters, and Deneb cannot set it. With highlighting off, Deneb tries to map highlight values onto the base measure names. Traps: (1) in the shipped 2.0.0.0, __highlightStatus and __highlightComparator are wrong for rows whose highlight value is null (fixed on main after the tag, deneb#753), so test __highlight for null instead. (2) Author enableHighlight true before the visual is first opened under 2.0; otherwise the migration freezes highlight:false in supportFieldConfiguration.

capabilities.topic: Power BI default tooltips from a Deneb mark
capabilities.detail: enableTooltips defaults to true. In Vega, encode 'tooltip': {'signal': 'datum'} or an object signal; in Vega-Lite, set mark tooltip true or a tooltip channel. Deneb hands key/value pairs to Power BI's tooltip service, so styling comes from the visual's Tooltip format card. There is no per-point styling: a custom-styled hover card like a vendor visual's has to be drawn as Vega marks. Default tooltips need no row context. Auto-formatting with the model format string only applies to NUMERIC fields whose key matches a Values field name. A Date object is not auto-formatted, so build the tooltip object with timeFormat(datum.Date, ...) or pbiFormat. tooltipDelay is 0-10000 ms. Sentence-template tooltips (Power BI, June 2026) can read only fields that are in the tooltip object. Modern tooltips can show drill-through actions.

capabilities.topic: Reading report theme colours (pbiColor and pbiColor* schemes)
capabilities.detail: pbiColor(index | name, shade) returns a theme data colour by 0-based index, or a named colour: min, middle, max, negative, neutral, positive, and the aliases bad and good. shade runs from -1 to 1 and darkens or lightens the colour. Schemes: pbiColorNominal is the data colours; pbiColorOrdinal and pbiColorLinear interpolate divergent min to max, without middle; pbiColorDivergent runs min, middle, max. The colours are read live, so a report theme change updates the visual. A sequential heatmap ramp built on pbiColorLinear therefore follows the theme's divergent min/max. For a fixed brand ramp, hard-code it or drive it from a measure. An unknown name falls through to theme colour index 1. No other theme property is reachable (foreground, background, text classes, fonts).

capabilities.topic: Detecting a dark theme or the background colour
capabilities.detail: Deneb binds host.colorPalette but exposes only data, divergent and sentiment colours to specs. Background, foreground and isHighContrast cannot be reached from an expression. The Power BI-flavoured config (theme foreground for text and axes) is baked in once, statically, when a spec is created from the built-in catalog, and is not re-read at runtime. Deneb forces config.background 'transparent', so the Power BI visual or page background shows through. Workarounds: (1) set the visual background in Power BI and pick text colours that suit it; (2) feed a theme flag or hex colours into the dataset from a measure (for example a disconnected 'Mode' table with a slicer) and switch palettes in the spec. Guessing the theme from pbiColor luminance is unreliable.

capabilities.topic: Container size signals and responsive sizing
capabilities.detail: In 2.0 the container is the denebContainer signal (Vega) or param (Vega-Lite): an object with width, height, scrollWidth, scrollHeight, scrollTop and scrollLeft. The legacy names pbiContainerWidth, pbiContainerHeight and pbiContainer work natively on 1.9, and 2.x rewrites them textually at parse time (deprecated, removal target 3.0). denebContainer does not exist on 1.9, where a spec using it is expected to fail to parse (inferred, not reproduced). Rule: use denebContainer.* only when the visual is stamped 2.0.0.0 or later; otherwise keep the legacy names. With autosize fit, Deneb sizes an unsized spec from the container, so do not write a literal width/height. Standard Vega-Lite layouts get 'container' automatically. A calendar can derive its cell size from the container, for example min((w - labels)/53, (h - gaps)/(7 * years)). A spec that overflows the container gets Deneb overlay scrollbars, and scrollTop/scrollLeft update the signal (throttle 5 ms by default), so a tall multi-year calendar can scroll.

capabilities.topic: Row limit, data limit override, and whether 10 years of daily data fits
capabilities.detail: The default window is 30,000 rows in 2.0 (capabilities.json dataReductionAlgorithm.window.count) and 10,000 in 1.9.1. A row is a distinct combination of grouping columns; measures add columns, not rows. 10 years x 365 days = 3,650 rows, which fits easily in both builds with several measures. Every added grouping column multiplies the rows: 8 categories x 3,650 = 29,200, which fits 2.0 only. dataLimit.override fetches more in 10,000-row batches, but only while a report is viewed; Microsoft no longer guarantees it during PDF/PPT export, so do not design around it. Supporting fields widen each row: on unstamped or migrated visuals every measure gets __format and __formatted.

capabilities.detail: Vega event streams accept {'type': 'timer', 'throttle': ms}. vega-view blocks a timer only if the view's eventConfig forbids it, and Deneb 2.0.0.0 sets no eventConfig (no match in the source). So a signal such as frame = playing ? frame + 1 : frame, updated on a timer, can drive playback, with a play/pause signal toggled by a clickable mark. Vega-Lite variable params have no 'on', so Vega-Lite cannot use a timer. A scrubber can be a Vega-drawn slider (drag signals) or a bound HTML input ({'bind': {'input': 'range'}}); in 2.0 a bound input is the only Tab-focusable element in the visual. Caveats: every tick re-runs the dataflow and re-renders, so with 3,650 marks use canvas and keep per-tick work to encode updates. Deneb reports renderingFinished when the embed completes, so an export captures the initial state; make the default state paused or showing everything. A new dataset from Power BI resets signal state unless continuous view patches it (threshold at most 5,000 rows). A timer signal parsed and ran offline in Vega 6.4.0; not tested in Desktop.

capabilities.topic: Custom fonts (Sora or any web font)
capabilities.detail: A spec can name any CSS font-family (config font, mark font), but it cannot load one. The certified build blocks every external resource, fonts included (the ALLOW_EXTERNAL_URI build flag is false), and a spec has no way to declare @font-face. Deneb bundles only DIN, registered as 'din' and 'wf_standard-font' (base64 in style/visual.less), and Segoe UI resolves on Windows clients. So 'Sora' renders only on machines with Sora installed locally; everywhere else, including Service-side export rendering, it falls back. Use a stack such as 'Sora, Segoe UI, sans-serif' and accept the fallback, or design in Segoe UI or DIN. The uncertified standalone build can fetch resources, but it loses PDF/PPT export and subscriptions.

capabilities.detail: 2.0 declares supportsKeyboardFocus. Enter moves focus into the visual, Tab cycles (and wraps) within Deneb's own UI, and Esc returns to the canvas. capabilities.topic: Screen-reader labels (aria / description on marks)
capabilities.detail: Vega marks accept the aria (boolean), description, ariaRole and ariaRoleDescription encode properties; Vega-Lite has the description channel and the aria mark property. The SVG renderer writes them out as aria-label and role attributes; offline in Vega 6.4.0, 3,650 rects produced 3,650 aria-label attributes. The canvas renderer creates no per-mark DOM, so it produces no labels, which means SVG versus canvas is also an accessibility trade-off. Marks cannot take focus, so screen-reader users can only reach them in browse/virtual mode, and 3,650 labelled cells is noisy. Consider aria false on the cells, a summary description on a group or axis, and the Power BI alt text on the visual container.

capabilities.topic: Performance of ~400 to 3,650 rect marks, SVG vs canvas
capabilities.detail: 400 to 3,650 rects is comfortably within Vega's range. Offline in Vega 6.4.0 (Node, no DOM), 3,650 rects with 3 formula transforms parsed and rendered to a 561 KB SVG in about 72 ms, and 400 rects in about 19 ms; a browser DOM will cost more. SVG gives crisp text, per-mark aria and pbiPatternSVG fills. Canvas avoids 3,650 DOM nodes and is the better choice once hover or animation re-renders every mark; pair it with stateManagement.scaleToZoom (2.0, canvas only) to reduce blur. Deneb recompiles the whole spec on each data update unless continuous view patches it (dataLimit.enableIncrementalDataUpdates, incrementalUpdateThreshold default 500, hard maximum 5,000). 3,650 rows is under that ceiling, but the docs warn Power BI may suspend a slow patch. Standard levers: aggregate in DAX, bind only the fields the spec reads, and on stamped 2.0 visuals switch off unused supporting fields.

capabilities.topic: Date parsing of Power BI dates and time-zone pitfalls
capabilities.detail: Dates work, with pitfalls. Deneb casts dateTime fields with new Date(value.toString()), so a date arrives as a JS Date at local midnight in the viewer's browser time zone (the local-midnight part is inferred and not observed in Desktop). Use local functions: in Vega, date, day, month, year, week, timeFormat and datetime; in Vega-Lite, the default local timeUnits. utc* functions, utcFormat, 'utc' scales and VL 'utc...' timeUnits shift the day for viewers east of UTC: offline in Australia/Sydney, utcdate != date for all 3,650 rows. Do not derive day or week indexes by dividing milliseconds by 864e5 without rounding, because DST days are 23 or 25 hours; generate missing days with datetime(y, m, d + i), not by adding 864e5. Cross-filter placeholders render a date as toDate('<ISO>'), which works for range tests; == never matches, so use time(). Vega week() starts on Sunday, and the isoweek timeunit only arrived with Vega 6.3 (the 2.0 bundle), so compute Monday-start weeks by hand to stay 1.9-compatible. Bind the raw date column, not the auto date/time hierarchy (in PBIR a Column projection, not a HierarchyLevel), or the dataset gets Year/Quarter/Month/Day columns (general Power BI behaviour, not verified in Deneb). Default tooltips do not auto-format Date values.

capabilities.topic: Other blocker: sparse days (blank measures drop rows)
capabilities.detail: The visual's query (SUMMARIZECOLUMNS) drops rows where every measure is blank, so days with no activity never arrive in the dataset. A calendar grid needs every day. There are two options. (1) Make the measure return 0, which delivers all 3,650 rows but loses the difference between zero and blank. (2) Generate the full date grid in the spec (Vega sequence plus a formula with datetime(...)) and look up the dataset values onto it. Generated cells have no __row__, so they get no report-page tooltip, context menu or cross-filter; only real rows are interactive. This comes from standard Power BI query behaviour and was not tested with Deneb specifically.

templateSteps: Branch first: main on InsightfulAnalytics/Deneb has the 'Protect main' ruleset (PR only, no direct push). History uses one conventional commit per part (feat:, fix:, docs(tools):), then a PR.

Folder: templates/<category>/<slug>/ holding <slug>.json, sample-data.csv, render.json, README.md and preview.png. check-templates.mjs only finds a template whose file basename equals its folder name. Existing categories are kpi, comparison, financial, gauge and map. A new one (for example calendar) is ordered after map on the showcase unless you add it to CATEGORY_ORDER in tools/showcase/build_showcase.py line 32.

Spec body (follow kpi-line-card): $schema is https://vega.github.io/schema/vega-lite/v6.json or .../schema/vega/v6.json. Top-level config is {autosize {type fit, contains padding}, view {stroke transparent}, background transparent, font 'Segoe UI'}; Vega specs also set text, guide-label and guide-title fonts. Vega-Lite uses padding 0, data {name: 'dataset'} and no literal width or height (the checker warns). Vega reads data[0] {name: 'dataset'} and sets width and height to {signal: pbiContainerWidth} / {signal: pbiContainerHeight}. Never reference denebContainer (Deneb 1.9 cannot parse it).

Options: every option is a top-level param (Vega-Lite: value or expr) or signal (Vega: value or update), with user options first and layout params after. Layout scales from a design size through a unit param, e.g. clamp(min(width / 264, height / 235), 0.5, 4), and every size, margin and baseline is N * unit. Colours use pbiColor('good'|'bad'|'neutral'), pbiColor('min'|'middle'|'max') or pbiColor(n, shade). Only text greys stay fixed hex. Numbers use d3 formats, not pbiFormat.

Tokens: the first transforms form an alias block that copies each datum['__n__'] into an internal name (toNumber(...), time(...)). Use bracket access only: datum.__0__ fails the checker. Every declared token must be used and every used token declared.

Dates are shown yyyy-mm-dd unless a value has a time. Numeric measure fields get an explicit measure 'Field (instance-id)' = SUM(...) with the raw column hidden. Column fields bind with summarizeBy none. The model is compat level 1606, en-US, auto date/time off, with no relationships and no date table. Each Deneb visual gets the template body without $schema or usermeta; config goes into jsonConfig with its font forced to Arial (any Segoe UI value is swapped too). Then params are applied by name, tokens are replaced by the dataset names, projections get displayName = the dataset name, stamps are Deneb 1.9.1 and the provider version, tooltips and context menu are on, selection and highlight off, render mode SVG, and container title, background, border, shadow and padding are off unless the slot turns them on.

risks: The report page is the main blocker. The generator supports exactly one multi-visual page (dashboard.json, always page 1, already the Gerard Duggan recreation and the README hero). make_background.py draws only that band/curve/grid geometry, and crop_previews.py writes every dashboard-kind page to showcase/dashboard.png, so a second one would overwrite the hero image. A page mimicking a web mockup needs build_showcase.py, make_background.py and crop_previews.py extended first. Hand-built pages are deleted on the next build.

'Looks the same' conflicts with locked decisions. There is one theme per report (BI Nexus), and Q18 locked 'no colour overrides anywhere'. The Q14 precedent restyles a recreated dashboard into BI Nexus colours and swaps the original logo. Matching the site's palette and branding would reopen Q18, or need a separate project.

Fonts: the generator forces Arial into every Deneb config and swaps any Segoe UI value. Template files ship Segoe UI. Deneb cannot load web fonts (the TE precedent swapped out Albert Sans), and textboxes can only use fonts installed on the machine. A web mockup's font (Inter or similar) will not match exactly.

Web chrome (sidebars, nav bars, rounded cards, icons, hover states, KPI tiles) has no native support. The generator emits only Deneb visuals, textboxes and images. Cards must come from the background SVG, from slot container border radius and shadow, or from Deneb. Slicers, buttons and native visuals are not generated. And because each instance gets its own unrelated table, a shared date slicer cannot filter the whole page.

Page size and capture: displayOption is hard-coded to FitToPage. A tall scrolling web page gets shrunk to fit the canvas, and the Desktop capture (scale 2 of the fitted canvas) then gives a low-resolution crop. Keep 16:9 (e.g. 1600 x 900). Also, crop_previews finds the canvas edge by scanning in from the right while pixels equal #F8FAFC (the Filters pane). A mockup with a slate-50 #F8FAFC page background, very common in web designs, would break the crop maths.

Big sample tables: build_showcase writes one DATATABLE line per row into the TMDL. 10k rows gives a TMDL of roughly 0.4 to 0.6 MB with heavy git diffs, and the checker warns when sample-data.csv is over 50 KB. Q6 says sample CSVs must hold only the rows the visual receives. Deneb receives the first 10,000 rows unless its data limit override is on, and the generator does not set it. Rendering is hard-coded to SVG, and 10k rect marks in SVG are slow. A calendar heatmap should ship one or two years of daily rows (365 to 731 rows, about 10 to 20 KB).

Calendar heatmap spec shape: Vega-Lite autosize fit works only for single or layered views, and the checker only sizes single views. A 12-month facet or concat calendar would not fit the container. The repo pattern is one layered Vega-Lite view with x and y computed from week and weekday offsets plus unit-scaled params, or Vega if labels need measured text. Watch date handling: the checker parses 'yyyy-mm-dd' as local midnight, so mixing utc* and local time functions can shift days by the AEST offset.

Interactivity: selection and highlight are false in usermeta by house convention, and hard-coded off in build_showcase.deneb_visual. A clickable calendar that cross-filters would need usermeta and generator changes.

IP and courtesy: lumericvisuals.com appears to sell custom visuals. Republishing a close copy of a commercial product as a free MIT template, and copying its report's look, is riskier than the TE blog precedent. Follow Q5: check their terms, write the spec from scratch with invented data, copy no images, code or branding, credit 'after Lumeric Visuals' in all five places, and draft a courtesy note before publishing. Not legal advice.

proto.interactivityWired:
Built on Deneb's advanced selection mode, which is Vega-only and is why the spec is Vega, not Vega-Lite. PBIR must set objects.vega enableSelection true, selectionMode 'advanced', enableTooltips true, enableContextMenu true and enableContextMenuSelector true. The signals:
1. downIdx and headIdx: both set to datum.idx on '@cell:mousedown'.
2. headIdx follows the drag on '[@cell:mousedown, window:mouseup] > @cell:mouseover'.
3. Both reset to null on 'view:mousedown[!event.item || event.item.mark.name !== \'cell\']'.
4. dragging: true on cell mousedown, false on window:mouseup.
5. selLo and selHi: min and max of downIdx and headIdx.
6. rangeFilter: builds the predicate string 'inrange(time(toDate(datum["Date"])), [<start of lo day ms>, <end of hi day ms>])'.
7. pbiCrossFilterSelection on 'view:mouseup': downIdx == null ? pbiCrossFilterClear() : pbiCrossFilterApply(event, rangeFilter, {limit: 400}).
A single click is a one-day range. A drag selects a contiguous date range in calendar order, not a rectangle. Ctrl or Shift add to the selection through Deneb's default multiSelect keys. A click on the background clears.
Feedback: while dragging, cells outside [selLo, selHi] drop to 0.28 opacity. Once Power BI applies the filter, each calendar day reads __selected__ from its looked-up dataset row (field 'sel'). The anySelected signal, fed by a selectedRows dataset, then dims every cell that is not 'on'. Each day also takes __row__ from its matched row, so tooltips and the context menu resolve (blank days have none). Tooltip: date plus pbiFormat(Sales, '#,0') or '(blank)'. Hovering a cell shows an ink outline.

disputes.evidence: Upgrade. The tooltip handler takes the identity from item.datum, not from the tooltip object: resolveDatumFromItem, then getResolvedRowIdentities. That accepts a copied __row__ if it is an in-range integer (data-point.ts 58-67) and passes it as identities to tooltipService.show (interactivity-manager.ts ~445). The prototype's tooltip object leaves out __row__ but still resolves. The only compromise cited (blank days) is a design choice, not a Deneb limit. Bind DimDate[Date] plus a helper measure that is non-blank for every date (e.g. COUNTROWS(DimDate)), or turn on 'Show items with no data'. Every day then arrives with a real __row__ and a null Sales value, so it draws empty and still gets the page tooltip. The Date formatting note is correct: getFieldsEligibleForAutoFormat only auto-formats numeric fields. Needs visualTooltip type 'Canvas'. Not tested in Desktop.

Downgrade from not-possible: two of the four parts have concrete mechanisms. (1) Keyboard. Deneb 2.0 supportsKeyboardFocus (Enter moves focus into the visual), and its handler intercepts only Tab (src/lib/keyboard-focus.ts), so arrow keys reach a Vega window:keydown stream (vega-view events() supports source 'window'). A focusIdx signal plus a ring mark gives arrow-key cell navigation. Enter can call pbiCrossFilterApply(event, "datum.Date == ..."), because a KeyboardEvent passes the instanceof Event gate and no placeholder is needed. Esc can call pbiCrossFilterClear(). (2) Screen reader. Vega 6 writes a per-item aria-label with role graphics-symbol from the 'description' encode channel (vega-scenegraph ariaItemAttributes), SVG renderer only. (3) High contrast is impossible: no isHighContrast or HC colours are exposed (Deneb registers only six expression functions; isHighContrast appears only in a dev theme shim). (4) Reduce motion is moot. Caveats: the focused cell is not announced (no aria-live), screen-reader browse mode captures arrow keys, SVG aria conflicts with the canvas advice for large data, and none of it is tested in Desktop.

Aggregates are fine, but the look is not reproducible exactly: KPI labels are uppercase with letter-spacing .1 to .11em (.kpi-k, .lp-kpi .k) and vega-scenegraph 6.4.0 has no letterSpacing text property at all (grep: 0 hits), and the values are Sora (--display, letter-spacing -.025em). By the same standard that made V12 approximate, this row is approximate.

Deneb 2.0 declares supportsKeyboardFocus (capabilities.md: Enter moves focus into the visual). Deneb's own document keydown listener only handles Tab wrap-around (apps/deneb/src/lib/keyboard-focus.ts handleTabWrapAround), so arrow keys should reach a Vega 'window:keydown' event stream: a focusIdx signal + drawn focus ring + Enter calling pbiCrossFilterApply(event, predicate) is buildable (2.0 only, untested in Desktop). SVG aria descriptions give partial screen-reader support. Only 'follow Windows high contrast' is truly impossible, so the bundled row is approximate, not not-possible.

The row admits the shadow is approximated. Site card shadow is two stacked layers with a negative spread (.shot.tight light: 0 1px 2px #17151d0d, 0 34px 70px -42px #17151d2e; el_light_rep.png shows it); a Power BI visual container has one shadow. missed: Real row context for blank days: bind DimDate[Date] plus a helper measure that is non-blank for every date (e.g. COUNTROWS(DimDate)), or use 'Show items with no data'. Blank days then get page tooltips, drill-through and click. The drag range also becomes the whole date span instead of only the days with data.
Prototype bug: the @cell:mousedown and view:mouseup signals have no [event.button === 0] filter, so a right-click (context menu or drill-through) also cross-filters the page to that day.
Touch and Power BI mobile: a mousedown/mouseover drag does not work on touch, so the range drag is desktop-mouse only and tap gives a single day.
macOS: advanced multiSelect accepts only ctrl, shift or alt (no meta), and ctrl-click opens the context menu on Mac, so 'ctrl-click to add' has to be shift-click there.
Multi-select semantics: selectionManager.select(ids, true) toggles, so a ctrl-drag over days already selected most likely removes them instead of adding the range.
A drag released outside the Deneb iframe never fires view:mouseup or window:mouseup, so the drag state sticks until the next click. Needs a reset path.
Keyboard cell navigation is buildable: window:keydown arrow keys drive a focusIdx signal and focus ring; Enter calls pbiCrossFilterApply with the KeyboardEvent; Esc calls pbiCrossFilterClear.
Per-cell screen-reader labels via the Vega 'description' encode (aria-label, SVG only). This trades off against the canvas recommendation for 10-year data.
Timer events cannot cross-filter at all (not instanceof Event). Only user mouse or keyboard events can, which limits the playback and animation ideas.

Top-level signals are usable inside the advanced filter string. The headless view is seeded with them, verified offline, so the range filter can reference selLo/selHi instead of concatenating epoch numbers.
Bookmarks can capture and restore the heatmap's selection (Deneb docs), which partly answers 'no persistence'.
2.0 continuous view (enableIncrementalDataUpdates) keeps signal state (playhead, drag, toggles) across cross-filter and slicer updates for datasets up to 5,000 rows.

Tooltip values: auto-format applies only to numeric fields whose tooltip value is the raw number. The prototype passes pbiFormat strings with a hard-coded '#,0', so model and dynamic format strings are ignored. Use Sales__formatted (opt-in via supportFieldConfiguration on stamped 2.0) or pass the raw number.
Sentence-template tooltips (June 2026) read only fields explicitly present in the tooltip object, so enumerate Date and Sales there.

Outbound range cross-filter carries only rows present in the heatmap's own dataset: days removed by an inbound filter cannot be selected, and without the helper measure blank days are never part of the filter.

Letter-spacing: Vega text marks have no letterSpacing property (vega-scenegraph 6.4.0), yet the site tracks every uppercase mono/display label (.kpi-k .1em, .lp-kpi .k .11em, .sk .14em). Inside Deneb this can only be faked by joining characters with hair spaces (split/join); affects V21, R10 to R13 and any in-spec card labels.

Font fallback for non-Windows viewers: Segoe UI and Consolas are not on macOS/iOS/Android, and a custom-visual iframe does not obviously inherit the host's web fonts (unverified). Ship a font stack in jsonConfig and preview on a Mac browser. The site's Win11 body font is 'Segoe UI Variable Text', which is also not plain Segoe UI.

Unverified Sora route: static display text could be drawn as an image mark whose data:image/svg+xml;base64 URI embeds a base64 WOFF subset of Sora (OFL licence), since Deneb's loader accepts that prefix. Heavy, static-text-only, and layout cannot measure it; worth a spike only if exact type matters.
Anchor-preserving step resampling: a naive {scheme, count} range drops the two end hexes; use extent [-1/(n-1), 1+1/(n-1)] (tested: 5 steps returns the exact Signature anchors).

Blank days as real rows: 'Show items with no data' on a DimDate[Date] column in the Values well could deliver empty days with __row__, restoring tooltips, drill-through and cross-filter on blank cells. Unverified in Deneb; generated blanks remain the safe default.

Pixel snapping at Dense gap 1px: fractional x/width values anti-alias into uneven, shimmering gaps (the site's CSS grid snaps). Round cell positions to whole or half pixels, or accept it; not called out in V04/V05.
Export plus overflow: PDF/PPT export and subscriptions capture only the visible viewport, so the V34 10-year scroll layout exports truncated. Exported layouts must fit the container.
Canvas crispness on 1.9.1: canvas mode (advised for 10-year/hover) has no scaleToZoom before 2.0, so capsule edges blur at report zoom on 1.9.1 viewers.

Small-multiple blanks: Vega's cross transform only crosses a stream with itself, so region x day cells must come from a sequence over nRegions*nDays indexed into a regions dataset (tested: 1,460 cells, 132 blanks).

Mock artefact: the product-page/full-canvas captures show one entirely absent week column right after the peak column (el_light_cvfull.png, compare-1to1.png top). It belongs to the widened-peak bug the matrix already flags; do not reproduce it.

Keyboard navigation (V39): Deneb 2.0 supportsKeyboardFocus plus a Vega window:keydown stream allows an arrow-key cell cursor with a drawn focus ring and Enter-to-filter. The matrix wrote this off as impossible.

Vega text marks have no letter-spacing property. The mock's KPI labels (.kpi-k .1em) and the full-canvas KPI labels are tracked uppercase mono. The workaround is hair-space joins or per-character marks at a fixed Consolas advance (0.55em). Only the rail keys can use SVG letter-spacing.

The font gap is smaller than the matrix says, but the repo makes it bigger. Only the page title (.rep-t), KPI values (.kpi-v) and hero/panel titles (.shot-t) use Sora. Body text is Segoe UI, and mono renders as Consolas on Windows, so most text could be exact. However, build_showcase.py forces FONT='Arial' on textboxes, to_arial() plus config font=Arial on every Deneb visual, and bi-nexus.json textClasses are Arial. An exact look needs a showcase font exception to Q18.

Untested route for static Sora text: a page-background SVG carrying a subset Sora (OFL) @font-face as a data URI could render the title and other static labels in Sora. It cannot help dynamic KPI values. It needs checking in Desktop and in the PDF export.

Colour token format: the site's alpha tokens are CSS #RRGGBBAA (--line2 #17151d0e, --empty #17151d0d), but PBIR 8-digit hex is ARGB (pbir-format expressions.md). Write container colours as '#0E17151D', or precomposite them; a pasted CSS value gives the wrong colour. Deneb/Vega accepts the CSS form.

Shadows: container_objects() emits only dropShadow show:true, which inherits the BI Nexus '*' custom navy shadow (#0B1E3F, blur 14, distance 2, 92% transparency). Tuning it to the mock's two-layer negative-spread shadows needs the generator to emit color, blur, distance and transparency, or a per-report theme.

BI Nexus theme defaults clash with the rail and pill look. actionButton has navy #0B3D91 fill with amber selected, advancedSlicerVisual has blue/amber accent bars, slicer has a bold 14pt navy header and #1E6FD9 outline, and '*' adds a #EEF4FB r8 border plus a shadow to every visual. There is no pageNavigator style. Restyling each native visual needs visual-level overrides that Q18 ('No colour overrides anywhere') forbids.
Q7 (templates theme-driven via pbiColor) means a Signature-hex default breaks the template rule itself, not only the showcase rule Q18. Under BI Nexus, pbiColor(0) = #1E6FD9.

v1 template usermeta (kept for the Background Designer harvest) cannot declare selectionMode 'advanced', so imported copies arrive in simple mode. Click and ctrl-click work in simple mode; drag-range needs a manual switch.

The generator writes no page visualInteractions. In a shared model, a click on the Sales heatmap would also filter the Tickets and Sessions heatmaps and Sales by month down to one day, unless interactions are set per pair in page.json.

The generator creates only SUM-of-column measures. Peak day (a date), Active days 289/364, mean per calendar day and the bullet target must be computed in-spec from daily rows, or the generator must accept authored DAX measures. The 364 denominator has to come from the date extent, because SUMMARIZECOLUMNS drops blank days.

Viewer-facing controls: native what-if (numeric range) parameter sliders, button slicers with per-button swatch images, and bookmarks can drive Deneb signals through measure fields. That makes working report-level lookalikes of the Studio, the drawer and the setup flow (R32-R35) possible.
A page navigator on the showcase would list the Duggan page and all 12 template pages. It must be limited to Daily overview, By region and Targets.
'Daily Sales · FY26' and 'Year · FY26' are static in the mock. Once the Year slicer works, a static or background-SVG title goes stale, and a dynamic title means a measure-driven textbox, so no Sora.

The DATE RANGE mini-calendar is a static aria-hidden 112x64 SVG: 7 columns, header bars, 5 rows and a fixed highlighted run. An exact copy is static decoration, and a working picker is a separate, visibly different native slicer.
